s1.syndrome_frame: Subcutaneous swellings with progressive enlargement over months, firm to hard, without pain, and with normal overlying skin
salient_findings: Bilateral neck masses and masses on the back and anterior abdominal wall
Firm to hard, nontender, mobile swellings
Cytology showing plump spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm
key_facts: 15-year-old girl presented with multiple swellings
Swellings have been progressively enlarging over five months
No pain associated with the swellings
Seven subcutaneous swellings were found on examination
Swellings were firm to hard and mobile
No changes in the overlying skin
Normal complete blood count, metabolic panel, and skeletal survey
FNAC showed moderate cellularity with similar features at all sites
Cytology smears showed predominantly plump spindle cells
Ultrasonography confirmed lesions were confined to subcutaneous tissue
No lymphadenopathy or deeper masses were found

shortlist.label: Desmoid tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Matches clinical presentation of firm, mobile, and progressive subcutaneous swellings

shortlist.label: Fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to desmoid tumor, with potential for local aggression and matching histological features

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: Characterized by subcutaneous growth and specific histological features, although less common in this age group

shortlist.label: Nodular fasciitis
shortlist.why_kept: Presents as a rapidly growing subcutaneous mass, which could fit the clinical picture, although typically less than 5 months duration

shortlist.label: Spindle cell lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Given the spindle cell morphology on FNAC, this entity remains a plausible, albeit less common, diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of multiple subcutaneous swellings with similar cytological features, predominantly plump spindle cells, and the absence of lymphadenopathy or deeper masses, are consistent with fibromatosis, a condition characterized by the growth of fibrous tissue in the subcutaneous layer.

rejected.label: Desmoid tumor
rejected.why: While desmoid tumors can present as firm, mobile masses, they are typically solitary and not multiple as seen in this case.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: This condition usually presents with a single, slowly growing mass and has distinct histological features not mentioned in the case.

rejected.label: Nodular fasciitis
rejected.why: Nodular fasciitis typically presents with a rapidly growing mass and has a distinct inflammatory component, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Spindle cell lipoma
rejected.why: Spindle cell lipoma is a type of benign tumor that typically occurs in the subcutaneous tissue of the neck or shoulder region, but it does not usually present with multiple masses as seen in this case.
